items.content:
Microsoft and Health-ISAC, along with the Japan Cybercrime Control Center (JC3) and a coalition of private sector companies, such as Resecurity, Cloudflare, Oracle, Proofpoint, and TRM Labs, announced the disruption of three phishing kits, CoGUI (aka NX or FA), Haozi (aka Phoenix), and Iron Man System .

"Since January 2026, the threat actors behind these kits have been responsible for facilitating the sending of over one billion phishing emails and SMS messages to over 75 thousand organizations worldwide," the Microsoft Threat Intelligence and Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit said .

The court-authorized operation is the result of an investigation that Microsoft launched in late 2025 after it was notified of malicious messaging campaigns targeting people in Japan. The

The Chinese-language cybercriminal ecosystem has been described as an interconnected network of phishing kit operators, developers, and an illicit marketplace and initial access broker (IAB) codenamed YAM Store that peddles tools and infrastructure using compromised or fraudulently obtained Microsoft or Google environments for large-scale phishing attacks.

Microsoft is tracking the underground marketplace as Storm-3119 and the developers behind all three phishing kits as Storm-2990. Evidence indicates that the three kits overlap in capabilities and infrastructure, suggesting shared development origins, code reuse, or close collaboration among their Chinese-speaking developers.

As is the case with any phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS or PaaS) platform, the end goal is to provide phishing templates impersonating legitimate brands and organizations spanning government, financial, and logistics sectors worldwide, and enable high-volume phishing and credential stealing operations.

"These messages have been used to target consumers, healthcare organizations, financial institutions, and other businesses in more than 150 countries, generating tens of millions of dollars for their operators," Health-ISAC said .

Threat actors are said to have purchased these phishing kits, along with access to compromised or fraudulent Microsoft or Google cloud environments, to target organizations across the healthcare, financial services, wholesale distribution, and information technology (IT) sectors in Japan, the U.S., Australia, and India.

"These phishing kits have been advertised through YAM Store, first CoGUI and Haozi, followed by Iron Man System starting in June 2026," Microsoft said. "YAM Store and affiliated phishing kit companies accepted payments through cryptocurrency, including USDT and Ethereum, adding another layer to conceal illicit activity."

YAM Store also occupies a central place in the operations, as it advertises legitimate infrastructure associated with legitimate, expired, or previously used organizations that other cybercriminals can purchase to attack their targets.

Some of the notable aspects of Storm-3119's tradecraft are listed below -

CoGUI, as detailed by Proofpoint in May 2025, has been observed targeting Japanese organizations by impersonating well-known consumer and finance brands such as Amazon, PayPay, MyJCB, Apple, Orico, and Rakuten. The kit is said to have been used in real-world campaigns since at least October 2024.

The phishing kit, per the enterprise security company, has also spawned two closely related variants named CoAceV and CoFish_Ws. In total, around 17,000 unique domains have been used by the three kits. By mid-2026, CoGUI was being increasingly replaced by Iron Man System, according to TRM Labs .

The Iron Man System features more than 2,335 phishing templates that are tailored to impersonate trusted brands and organizations across 139 countries, including Australia, Japan, India, and the U.S., while taking steps to restrict access to phishing content to only users from specific countries.

개별 서비스로 나뉘어 있던 구독 체계를 통합해 사용자 선택의 폭을 넓히고, 오픈AI와 앤트로픽 등 경쟁사와의 유료 AI 시장 경쟁에서 우위를 확보하려는 전략이다.

새 구독 상품은 그록의 AI 채팅 기능과 에이전트형 AI 봇, 커서의 AI 코딩 기능을 제공한다. 그록은 음성·이미지·동영상 입력과 API를 지원한다. X 프리미엄에 포함됐던 파란색 인증 마크, 크리에이터 도구, 광고 감소 등 유료 기능도 함께 이용할 수 있다.

요금제는 무료, 플러스(월 8달러), 프리미엄(월 30달러), 슈퍼(월 100달러), 울트라(월 200달러) 등 5단계로 구성된다. 상위 요금제로 갈수록 AI 사용 한도가 늘어난다. 무료 요금제에서는 채팅과 에이전트 기능을 제한적으로 이용할 수 있으며, 최신 그록 모델을 사용하려면 프리미엄 이상에 가입해야 한다.

기존 유료 구독자에게는 요금 부담을 줄일 수 있다는 점도 강조했다. 기존 X 프리미엄 플러스 사용자가 통합 상품으로 전환하면, 이에 상응하는 요금제가 기존과 같거나 더 저렴할 수 있다.

기존 사용자는 X의 구독 설정에서 새 상품으로 전환하거나 현재 요금제를 그대로 유지할 수 있다. 다만 업그레이드 옵션은 차례로 제공되므로, 전환을 원하는 사용자는 결제 설정에서 해당 옵션이 표시되는지 확인해야 한다.

이번 통합은 AI 서비스 구독 시장의 경쟁이 치열해지는 가운데 나왔다. 챗봇과 코딩 도구, 소셜미디어 유료 기능을 각각 판매하는 대신 하나의 구독 상품으로 묶어 이용자당 서비스 활용도를 높이고 장기 구독을 유도하려는 것이다.

특히 AI 챗봇과 코딩 도구를 함께 제공하면 일반 사용자뿐 아니라 개발자 수요까지 확보할 수 있다.

items.title: OCC report finds debanking efforts tied to crypto activities
items.summary: The report from the US banking regulator did not include specific examples of debanking related to crypto, but mentioned it alongside ties to oil, gas and firearms.
items.content:
The report from the US banking regulator did not include specific examples of debanking related to crypto, but mentioned it alongside ties to oil, gas and firearms.

The US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released a report on debanking efforts, including ties to digital assets as activities that influenced banks to limit financial services.

In a report released Wednesday, the OCC said certain banks had “public and nonpublic policies” restricting services for many industries, including oil and gas, tobacco, firearms and digital assets. According to the banking regulator, the report was in accordance with an August 2025 executive order from US President Donald Trump to prevent what he called “unlawful debanking.”

“Many institutions also placed restrictions on banking digital asset activities, including on issuers, exchanges, or administrators, often attributed to financial crime considerations,” said the OCC.

In November 2024, more than 30 tech and crypto executives claimed to have been denied access to banking services. Many in the crypto industry unofficially dubbed the effort as “Operation Chokepoint 2.0” after the Obama-era initiative to fight fraud and money laundering facilitated by banks.

However, Wednesday’s 47-page report did not include specific examples of debanking relating to digital asset activities. The OCC said it had been “unable to quantify on a comprehensive basis the full extent of debanking or alleged debanking actions” based on a review of nine major banks, and the agency’s head, Jonathan Gould, focused largely on the report’s claims around debanking due to ties to coal and firearms.

“These decisions were not based on financial risk,” said Gould, referencing the debanking due to connections to coal. “Instead, banks cited concerns about negative headlines, public protests, and the perceived reputational consequences of supporting the industry.”

The 2025 executive order from Trump followed calls from many in the industry surrounding claims -- including “Operation Chokepoint 2.0” -- that the US government under former President Joe Biden may have influenced financial institutions into cutting off crypto firms from certain services.

items.title: Spyware manufacturer had access to data harvested by former Polish government, current PM says
items.summary: Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who ordered the investigation, on Monday called the sprawling spyware operation spearheaded by the country’s previous ruling party “one of the biggest scandals in Polish history since the fall of communism.”
items.content:
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Image: European Union Spyware manufacturer had access to data harvested by former Polish government, current PM says

Polish investigators said they found evidence showing a spyware manufacturer harvested data from Polish opposition leaders and other victims and transmitted it to Israel.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who ordered the investigation, on Monday called the sprawling spyware operation spearheaded by the country’s previous ruling party “one of the biggest scandals in Polish history since the fall of communism.” He accused Israel-based NSO Group, the spyware manufacturer involved in the scandal, of collaborating with Israeli intelligence services.

Tusk’s comments came shortly after Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office said an analysis by the Internal Security Agency (ABW) had found Poland’s Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (CBA) — which ran the spyware program — “did not have full control over the Pegasus system” that NSO Group operated.

“The server module responsible for infecting mobile devices remained under the manufacturer's exclusive control,” the prosecutor’s office said in a press release.

The CBA also did not have passwords to access many accounts with administrative privileges, according to the press release.

“This prevented full verification of the correct functioning of individual system modules, including those responsible for data transmission and storage,” the press release said.

The data collected by the spyware company’s software was sent outside of Poland by an anonymizing network relying on servers located abroad, prosecutors said. The Polish probe found that data was transmitted via foreign IP addresses.

NSO therefore had “technical access” to information gathered from operational inspections, the press release said. Updates and technical support were supplied to Polish officials through a remote connection.

“During this work, operational inspections were not interrupted, and the manufacturer had full access to the system, including the ability to make changes to its software and configuration,” the press release said.

Polish investigators cannot say if NSO “actually obtained access to materials from specific operational inspection,” according to prosecutors.

A spokesperson for NSO Group did not respond to a request for comment.

In February 2024, Tusk’s government announced investigators had confirmed Pegasus was used to target a “very long” list of victims. Tusk revealed his own wife and daughter were spied on and that devices belonging to more than 500 others were targeted and, in some cases, infected.

Several former intelligence and security officials are facing charges for facilitating the spyware abuses, which were allegedly paid for by misappropriating a government fund meant to be spent on crime victims.

In a searing critique of the former officials behind the Pegasus deployment, Tusk reportedly said “they paid money for a system that de facto transferred all possible data on Polish citizens, Polish opposition leaders and Polish independent prosecutors…to the Israeli side.”

“This is no longer [just] a scandal… We’re talking about a crime against the state.”

The findings show that countries using spyware have to be worried about operational security, Citizen Lab researcher John Scott-Railton said in an interview with Recorded Future News.

NSO has long promised government customers it can’t access data collected by Pegasus, but Railton said discovery materials made public in a lawsuit WhatsApp filed against the spyware company in 2019 support the Polish government’s claims.

items.content:
반도체 설계 기업 Arm이 퀄컴과의 소송에서 불리한 평결을 받았다. 배심원단은 계약 위반과 사업 방해를 인정했으나, 손해배상금은 명목상 금액인 2달러만 부과했다.

미국 델라웨어주 배심원단은 13일(현지시간) 5일간의 재판 끝에 이같이 평결했다. 이번 공방은 소프트뱅크의 지배권 확보 이후 자체 칩 판매 영역으로 갈등이 깊어진 배경에서 비롯됐다.

배심원단은 소프트웨어 패치 및 설계 도구 제공 의무 위반을 인정했으나, 나머지 5건의 위반 주장은 기각했다. 또 Arm이 메타와의 계약 체결을 앞둔 퀄컴의 협상을 고의로 방해했다는 주장을 받아들여, 방해 2건에 각 1달러, 계약 위반 1달러를 합산해 총 2달러의 배상금을 산정했다.

양사는 각자 유리한 대목을 강조했다. 퀄컴은 오랜 계약 위반과 사업 방해 행위가 명확히 인정됐다고 환영했지만, Arm은 수십억달러 규모의 부당한 청구 속에서 단 2달러의 배상금만 나온 것은 자사 주장의 정당성을 입증하는 것이라고 맞섰다.

향후 재판부의 판단에 따라 5년간 로열티 지급 면제 여부 및 추가 항소 가능성 등 쟁점이 이어질 전망이다. 평결 직후 Arm 주가는 약 1% 하락했고, 퀄컴 주가는 약 1% 상승했다.

items.title: Kalshi CEO says state-led oversight of U.S. prediction markets would push them out
items.content:
ARLINGTON, Va. — The CEO of Kalshi, the company at the center of a high-profile legal battle over the future of prediction markets in the U.S., said the clash won't ultimately decide whether the rapidly growing industry is overseen by states or a federal agency, but whether it's overseen by the feds here or is forced overseas.

"We feel pretty good about where we stand overall," Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour said Wednesday at the DC Fintech Week event near Washington.

Mansour rejected arguments that sports betting — the explosively growing element of the event-contracts space — doesn't have significant economic consequences that justify the trades' status as federally regulated financial contracts.

"The notion that sports does not have economic consequence is ludicrous," he said.

A growing list of states have challenged Kalshi and other prediction markets firms in court, accusing them of engaging in illegal sports wagering that belongs under the authority of state gambling regulators. But Kalshi and the federal regulator of its exchange, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, have countered in courts that the federal agency is the appropriate sole watchdog of prediction markets.

So far, the dispute has risen to a number of federal appellate courts, where the courts have now split, with one major ruling on Kalshi's side and two backing the states' view. As a result, New Jersey asked the U.S. Supreme Court to take the case, and prominent groups have been sharing their views with the high court, including the National Football League .

Mansour said, "It's not a choice of state versus federal market. It's a choice of whether prediction markets exist in the U.S. or whether they go offshore."

He argued that he's considered Kalshi's regulatory relationship since its beginnings, and "it really elegantly fit under definitions of commodity." He said the Commodity Exchange Act was a "truly beautiful statue" that allowed a shift from agricultural futures to oil and metals to less tangible financial products like swaps.

Mansour also responded Wednesday to accusations of inflated trading volume in bitcoin and ether perpetual-futures markets on his platform. He said that "there's a lot of crazy" on social media site X, formerly Twitter. The questions focused on often-recurring trade sizes that represented a significant portion of Kalshi's volume. Mansour pointed again at the Washington event to fixed-size orders from market makers.

"Twitter went, like, 'Oh my God, there's a spike. There must be, you know, like inflation of volume or anything like that.' It's none of it," he said.

"Maybe the broader point about this is how much people misunderstand markets," he said. "They're just complicated. They're not easy to understand."

The CFTC has been making rapid moves to bolster its prediction markets authority. Last week, it issued a rule and proposed another that were meant to place event contracts into the definition of swaps that are explicitly policed by the agency and not by state gambling regulators.

The indictment charges a mix of U.S. citizens and Chinese nationals for their roles in an IT worker conspiracy affecting more than 70 U.S. companies, charging them with wire fraud conspiracy, money laundering conspiracy, conspiracy to commit identity theft, and aggravated identity theft.

The following individuals have been charged -

The two U.S. nationals, Carrillo and Bostelle, have been arrested, while the rest remain at large. The fraudulent scheme was operational from around 2019 to July 2025. Another key U.S.-based co-conspirator, Trey Michael Nolte, has been named in the indictment but was not charged.

Nolte is alleged to have managed a shell company called Dark Falls LLC that claimed to offer software development services, but was in fact used to perpetrate the criminal scheme. The operation also included the dismantling of more than 40 so-called laptop farms across Texas during raids that were conducted between September 21 and 25, 2026.

"Threats posed by nation-states like North Korea are a stark reminder that our adversaries will go to great measures to exploit our nation's economic strength to further and fuel their own nefarious agendas," said U.S. Attorney David M. Toepfer for the Northern District of Ohio.

Court documents allege that the defendants colluded to participate in a multi-year fraudulent scheme to land remote IT work to generate illicit revenue for the government of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), in violation of international sanctions and to fund its nuclear weapons and other military programs.

The operation, also tracked as Famous Chollima, purpledelta, and Wagemole , revolves around North Korean IT workers getting hired at American and other companies using fake identities, drawing regular salaries, a chunk of which is funneled back to the regime.

These workers are assisted by facilitators in the U.S. to help them get hired, host company-issued laptops at their residences, and leverage remote-access technology to make overseas workers appear to be legitimate U.S.-based employees.

The U.S. facilitators are also responsible for setting up accounts at U.S. banks and online money transfer services to enable the movement of money paid by U.S. victim companies to the IT workers and other persons located abroad. In return for these services, the facilitators are paid a fee.

In all, the scheme impacted more than 70 U.S. company employers and generated approximately $3 million in revenue for IT workers.

"Victim entities included companies serving a broad array of industries and services including health care, communications, cyber support, retail, and manufacturing companies," the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) said.

"Victim businesses were located not only in Ohio, but also across much of the U.S., including in Massachusetts, California, New York, New Jersey, Florida, Georgia, Minnesota, Maryland, North Carolina, Illinois, Virginia, Michigan, Texas, Arkansas, Pennsylvania, Washington, and the District of Columbia."

The effort is the latest by the U.S. in a long-running and intensifying campaign that aims to cut off a revenue-generation source and dismantle an evolving cyber threat from North Korea whose scale is likely vast.

Cybersecurity company CrowdStrike, which investigated indicators associated with suspected fake IT workers and identified links between apparently unrelated employees and laptop-hosting locations, said the threat actors have resorted to a variety of techniques to direct employer-provided hardware to laptop farm addresses during the onboarding phase.

items.content:
광양만권경제자유구역청(청장 구충곤)은 14일부터 16일까지 사흘간 부산 벡스코(BEXCO)에서 열리는 ‘2026 국제해양에너지플랜트산업전’에 참가해 투자유치 활동을 펼친다고 밝혔다.

‘2026 국제해양에너지플랜트산업전’은 산업통상자원부와 부산시가 주최하는 국내 유일의 조선·해양에너지플랜트 전문 산업전시회이다.

이번 산업전시회에는 글로벌 조선사를 비롯한 15개국 170여 개 기업이 참가해 600개 부스를 운영하며, 조선·해양플랜트, 해양에너지, 관련 기자재 등으로 친환경·탈탄소 기술과 AI, 자동화 등 산업의 디지털 전환 분야의 기술과 제품을 선보인다.

광양경자청은 해양에너지플랜트 분야 입주 앵커기업과 공동 홍보부스를 마련해 세풍·황금산단, 하동지구 갈사만산단 등 광양만권의 우수한 산단 투자환경과 입주 여건을 집중 홍보한다.

특히 홍보 부스에서는 현대스틸산업의 해상풍력 관련 제품 모형과 엠에스엘테크놀로지의 해상풍력 연계 시스템 등을 전시해 광양만권의 해양에너지플랜트 산업 경쟁력을 알린다.

현재 광양만권에는 현대스틸산업을 비롯해 한화오션에코텍, EEW, 세아제강, 현대제철, 한라IMS, DSR제강, 씨에스에너지 등 다양한 해양에너지플랜트 연관 기업이 입주해 탄탄한 산업 생태계를 구축하고 있다.

구충곤 광양경자청장은 “광양만권은 우수한 항만 인프라와 안정적인 공급망, 기업 친화적 환경을 두루 갖춘 해양에너지플랜트 산업의 최적지이다”라며 “이번 전시회를 발판 삼아 유망 기업들을 적극적으로 유치하고 광양만권의 미래 성장 동력을 확보해 나가겠다”고 말했다.

items.content:
구글이 안드로이드 사용자를 대상으로 정식 개발자 등록 절차 없이, 플레이 스토어를 통해 AI로 제작한 자신만의 맞춤형 애플리케이션을 간편하게 실행할 수 있는 새로운 생태계 혁신을 단행했다.

구글은 13일(현지시간) 공식 블로그를 통해 플레이 스토어 업데이트를 공개하며, 일반 사용자들이 구글 AI 스튜디오(Google AI Studio)를 활용해 '바이브 코딩' 방식으로 만든 맞춤형 안드로이드 앱을 플레이 스토어를 통해 간편하게 실행할 수 있게 된다고 밝혔다.

이번 조치로 복잡한 코딩 지식이나 유료 개발자 계정 등록 없이도 누구나 모바일 앱을 직접 만들고 실험할 수 있는 길이 열렸다. 기존에는 안드로이드 스마트폰에 앱을 설치하려면 개발자 등록 후 플레이 스트어에 앱을 등록하고 다운로드받아야 했다. 이 때문에 일부 개발자는 이런 번거로운 과정이 없는 웹 기반 플랫폼이나 다른 경로를 활용하는 데 집중해 왔으나, 이번 조치로 이러한 제약이 크게 해소될 것으로 전망된다.

새롭게 도입되는 개인용 앱은 완전한 비공개 상태로 유지된다. 구글 플레이의 공개 검색 결과나 추천 목록 등에 노출되지 않으며, 오직 제작자 본인만 이용할 수 있다. 다만, 플랫폼의 안전성을 담보하기 위해 구글 플레이의 기존 보안 정책은 엄격하게 준수해야 한다.

샘 브라이트 구글 플레이 및 개발자 생태계 부사장은 "구글 플레이 앱의 미래는 개인 맞춤형이고, 안전하며, 누구나 참여할 수 있는 형태로 진화하고 있다"라며, "플레이가 단순히 기존 앱과 연결해 주는 공간을 넘어 사용자 개개인에게 꼭 맞는 맞춤형 플랫폼으로 도약하고 있음을 보여준다"고 강조했다.

구글은 이후 사용자가 직접 만든 바이브 코딩 앱을 신뢰하는 친구나 가족 등 소규모 그룹과 공유할 수 있도록 기능을 확대할 계획이다. 또 소규모 그룹 내에서 검증을 거친 인기 앱은 향후 신뢰성 및 안전성 검토를 거쳐 정식으로 플레이 스토어에 공개 출시할 수 있는 전환 절차도 마련될 예정이다.

한편, 구글은 이번 업데이트를 통해 AI 기반의 개인화 기능과 게임 검색 편의성도 대폭 강화했다. 영어권 사용자들을 시작으로 개인의 취향과 커뮤니티 데이터를 분석해 최적의 게임을 추천하는 '게임 파인더(Game Finder)' 기능이 도입되며, 플레이 스토어 내부의 AI 비서 '애스크 플레이(Ask Play)'를 통해 유사 앱 간의 주요 기능을 직관적으로 비교할 수 있게 지원한다.

items.content:
AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary. ( via ) Indie game developer Popcar talks about the recent wave of AI-powered decompilation of existing games, enabling weird mashups between existing games, and producing a boom in game preservation projects to get old games working on new hardware (often in a browser using WebAssembly).

I like how this piece captures both the positives and the negatives of this new development:

Most people already realized the scary part by now. If AI can decompile games and software, then the entire tech industry is about to explode. Anybody can decompile other software and use it any way they'd like, and nobody can stop them. Companies can steal from competitors. Your paid game or app can be open-sourced against your will. This isn't exclusive to old video games, we can apply this to  any  software. [...]

This is also a big win for preservation. Old games can be ported, modified, enhanced, and made much more easily accessible than before. [...[

With console makers going all in on digital and games becoming entirely unplayable due to servers shutting down, this is  fantastic  news. We could own software we bought regardless of what the company thinks.

items.title: AI Agents Navigate Unfamiliar OT Systems and Move Equipment in Minutes, Booz Allen Finds
items.summary: In Booz Allen’s isolated OT lab, AI models met every objective across eight scenarios and reached an industrial control network from a perimeter compromise in just over 16 minutes. The post AI Agents Navigate Unfamiliar OT Systems and Move Equipment in Minutes, Booz Allen Finds a
items.content:
A new report from Booz Allen demonstrates that “frontier super intelligence navigated unfamiliar industrial systems, adapted when blocked, and moved physical equipment within minutes.”

The findings of the report were presented last week at SecurityWeek’s Industrial Control Systems (ICS) Cybersecurity Conference in Nashville, ahead of the public release.

Use of the term ‘super intelligence’ is, however, confusing. This is not the first time the firm has used it, but it seems to be indistinguishable from the more common term of artificial intelligence (AI). It also quickly follows Donald Trump’s September 29, 2026 Executive Order to “replace the term ‘Artificial Intelligence’ (‘AI’) with ‘Super Intelligence’ (‘SI’) in the executive branch.”

The problem, however, is that ‘superintelligence’ (one word) has long been used for a specific quality of AI. It was defined by Oxford philosopher Nick Bostrom in 2014 as, ‘Any intellect that greatly exceeds the cognitive performance of humans in virtually all domains of interest.’ It is consequently more akin or superior to artificial general intelligence (AGI), which is in turn superior to common or garden AI.

So, is Booz Allen referring to frontier AI in line with Trump’s executive order, or something more advanced in line with Bostrom’s ‘superintelligence’? The world of AI is suffering from a lack of consistent and formal definitions; but we’ll assume that Booz Allen is using ‘super intelligence’ to indicate the improving capabilities of contemporary artificial intelligence rather than a new type of AI. ( SecurityWeek reached out to Booz Allen for clarification on the terminology but had received no response at the time of writing.)

The firm examined the potential effect of AI agents on OT using AI frontier models within its own isolated OT lab. These agents were given no prior knowledge of the OT in question: neither source code, nor engineering documents, nor advanced OT guidance. While the firm’s OT environment isn’t necessarily identical to enterprise OT, it is a reasonable representation. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

“Across eight scenarios, every defined test objective was achieved. More important, the models connected work that usually spans multiple people and stages, including asset discovery, device research, attack planning,” summarize the researchers. More specifically, it took little more than 16 minutes for models in one test to move from a perimeter compromise to actions inside an industrial control network. In another test, a model found a robotic arm, mapped its protection zones and motion limits, and moved it within minutes.

Noticeably, within these tests, existing defenses blocked or slowed some actions, but no single safeguard consistently stopped the autonomous models from achieving their objectives.

The full Booz Allen whitepaper explains, “We have long understood that non-kinetic cyber actions can produce kinetic effects. What has changed is the speed and precision with which these models can help produce those kinetic effects. They also undermine the ‘security through obscurity’ approach on which many operational technology (OT) environments have long relied.”

items.content:
팔로알토 네트웍스는 14일 서울 강남구 웨스틴 파르나스 하모니볼룸에서 ‘이그나이트 온 투어 서울’을 개최하고 AI 시대 기업의 보안 대응 전략을 공유했다. 행사에서는 AI 기반 위협에 대응하기 위한 선제적 방어, 제로 트러스트, 보안관제 자동화, 아이덴티티 보안 등이 주요 과제로 제시됐다.

‘프론티어 AI 디펜스’를 주제로 열린 이번 행사에는 BJ 젠킨스 팔로알토 네트웍스 사장이 방한해 기조연설을 진행했다. 회사는 AI 시스템의 설계 단계부터 보안을 반영하는 ‘시큐어 AI 바이 디자인(Secure AI by Design)’과 통합 보안 아키텍처를 중심으로 기업의 보안 전환 방향을 설명했다.

박상규 팔로알토 네트웍스 코리아 대표이사는 개막 기조연설에서 AI와 자율형 에이전트가 공격의 속도와 방식을 바꾸고 있다며, 기업 보안 체계를 전반적으로 재정비하는 ‘사이버보안 트랜스포메이션(CX)’의 필요성을 강조했다.

박 대표는 일회성 취약점 점검을 넘어 위협에 노출된 지점을 지속적으로 파악하고 개선해야 한다고 설명했다. 보안 전문가와 협력해 취약점의 실제 악용 가능성을 검증하고, 사고 예방부터 대응·복구까지 연결하는 역량을 갖춰야 한다는 것이다.

또한 제로 트러스트와 AI 기반 통합 보안관제, 자동화를 함께 추진하고 보호 범위를 사람뿐 아니라 머신과 AI 에이전트의 아이덴티티까지 확대해야 한다고 밝혔다. 개별 솔루션으로 분산된 보안 체계를 통합해 사각지대와 운영 복잡성을 줄이는 방안도 제시했다.

박 대표는 “AI 기반 공격에 대응하기 위해서는 기존 보안 체계를 전반적으로 재정비하는 사이버보안 트랜스포메이션을 지금 시작해야 한다”며 “10가지 핵심 실행 이니셔티브를 중심으로 제로 트러스트와 보안 운영 자동화, AI 보안 도입을 함께 추진하고, 플랫폼화를 통해 기업 전반의 보안 역량을 높여야 한다”고 말했다.

젠킨스 사장은 ‘AI 기업의 현재와 미래를 위한 보안’을 주제로 기업의 AI 도입과 공격 자동화에 따른 보안 과제를 설명했다. 기업이 AI를 보조 도구에서 자율형 에이전트로 확장하는 가운데, 공격자도 AI를 이용해 공격 과정을 자동화하면서 대응에 주어진 시간이 줄고 있다는 진단이다.

팔로알토 네트웍스가 행사에서 인용한 유닛 42의 ‘2026 글로벌 사고 대응 보고서’에 따르면, 최초 침해부터 데이터 유출까지 걸리는 시간은 2024년 4.8시간에서 2026년 1.2시간, 약 72분으로 단축됐다. 회사는 신규 취약점이 15분 만에 악용되는 사례도 제시하며 대응 속도의 중요성을 강조했다.

젠킨스 사장은 “공격 주기가 압축되면서 머신 속도로 이뤄지는 AI 공격을 사람의 속도로는 따라잡을 수 없다”며 “통합은 AI 시대 효과적인 보안을 위한 전제 조건이며, 기업은 네트워크부터 아이덴티티 계층까지 아우르는 보안 기반을 마련해야 한다”고 말했다.

전문가 세션과 패널토의에서는 회사 전문가와 고객사 관계자들이 보안 기술과 도입 경험을 공유했다. AI 보안 제품 ‘프리즈마 AIRS’, 보안 운영 및 관측성 제품군 ‘코어텍스’, 아이덴티티 보안 ‘아이디라’를 중심으로 보안 도구의 분산을 줄이고 운영을 자동화하는 방안이 소개됐다.

items.title: ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens Issues 17 Advisories, Rockwell Fixes ArmorBlock Takeover Flaw
items.summary: ABB previously published an advisory warning about possible probing of a dynovaPRO vulnerability. The post ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens Issues 17 Advisories, Rockwell Fixes ArmorBlock Takeover Flaw appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
Industrial giants Siemens, Schneider Electric, and Rockwell Automation have published ICS security advisories this Patch Tuesday.

Siemens published 17 new advisories this Patch Tuesday. The company has released patches for some of the vulnerabilities, while for others it has shared mitigations until permanent fixes become available.

The company addressed critical vulnerabilities in some Simatic S7-1500 CPUs, Industrial Edge devices, and the Ruggedcom Crossbow Station Access Controller (SAC). For Simatic CPUs, more than 400 flaws affect the GNU/Linux subsystem.

Siemens addressed high-severity issues in Ruggedcom Crossbow, Simatic IPC, PSS(R)SINCAL, the .NET Client Library for Simatic S7 Webserver API, Industrial Edge App Publisher, Apogee, Desigo, Talon, Ruggedcom APE1808, and Simatic WinCC products.

Medium-severity issues have been patched in Sentron 3NA COM Fuse and Capital Embedded AR Classic.

Siemens also informed customers about a documentation ambiguity affecting Simatic S7 PLCs and related products. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Schneider Electric released two new advisories, each covering one high-severity vulnerability. The first affects Pro-face STW6000 and Harmony STW6 and could allow an attacker to take control of a device by tricking the targeted user into visiting a malicious webpage.

The second affects Sage RTUs and it can be leveraged by a privileged user to install malicious firmware on a device.

Rockwell Automation published one new advisory on Tuesday. It informs customers about two vulnerabilities in 1732E ArmorBlock.

One of them, rated ‘critical’, allows an unauthenticated attacker to change a device’s web server password, which can lead to admin account takeover. The second flaw is a DoS issue.

CISA published two new ICS advisories on Tuesday: one covers Swann SWIFI-SE2KIC camera vulnerabilities exposing video information, and the other covers a privilege escalation issue in Inductive Automation’s Ignition product.

Germany’s CERT@VDE has published one new advisory to inform organizations about an information disclosure vulnerability affecting Bender’s Customer&Partner platform.

Between this and the previous Patch Tuesday, advisories were published by Moxa (two severe protocol gateway vulnerabilities), Honeywell (Pro-Watch), Hitachi Energy (Asset Suite, RTU500, MicroSCADA), Johnson Controls (ADVMS, Illustra Standard, EasyIO), and ABB (Automation Builder, Mint Workbench, AC500, Protection and Control IED Manager, Freelance, and dynovaPRO).

Regarding the dynovaPRO vulnerability , which could allow account takeovers via a bypass in the credential reset flow, ABB said it’s not aware of any in-the-wild exploitation, but added: “Internal log analysis identified 26 password change events affecting 9 customers, which may indicate testing or reconnaissance activity.”

Organizations should closely monitor CISA and CERT@VDE, which regularly publish ICS advisories.

items.content:
Microsoft fixes VPN issues caused by September Windows updates

Microsoft has resolved a known issue that caused Always On VPN connection issues after installing the September 2026 Windows 11 security updates.

The Always On VPN remote access solution replaced the legacy DirectAccess technology and works with domain-joined, non-domain-joined, and Microsoft Entra ID–joined Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server devices.

Always On VPN runs in the background and automatically establishes a secure tunnel back to the corporate network whenever a device connects to the internet.

As Microsoft first acknowledged in a service alert sent to IT administrators in late September, the bug triggered Always On VPN failures if the initial connection fails (e.g., when using automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP) on up-to-date systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later.

On Tuesday, the company released the KB5127648 and KB5127646 cumulative updates that address this known issue on all affected systems.

"When automatic protocol selection or protocol fallback was configured, affected VPN connections could remain stuck in a Connecting state or fail to connect after an initial connection attempt failed," it said . "In some cases, subsequent connection attempts could display the error, 'The specified port is already in use.'"

Microsoft has also shared a temporary fix for customers who can't immediately install the October 2026 Patch Tuesday update, which requires them to choose one of two VPN tunneling protocols to work around the issue.

"IT administrators can mitigate this issue by changing the Always On VPN profile from automatic protocol selection to a single protocol, either SSTP only or IKEv2 only, depending on their environment and configuration," Microsoft said. "Organizations should select the protocol based on their environment, security, and deployment requirements."

Last month, it released emergency updates to fix Remote Desktop Services failures , Hyper-V issues , and USB audio problems affecting home and enterprise Windows users, which were also triggered by the September 2026 updates.

This week, it also confirmed that non-admin users may have issues connecting to devices via Remote Desktop after installing recent Windows updates if the "Administrator protection" security feature is enabled.

items.content:
인섹시큐리티(대표 김종광)는 국내 총판을 맡고 있는 옵스왓(OPSWAT)이 국가망보안체계(N²SF) 전환에 대응하기 위한 ‘소프트웨어 공급망 통합 보안 플랫폼’을 발표했다고 14일 밝혔다.

이번 플랫폼은 소프트웨어를 개발하고 배포하는 과정부터 업무 파일 전송, 서로 다른 보안 수준의 네트워크 간 데이터 이동까지 보안 검증을 연계하는 것이 핵심이다. 소프트웨어의 구성요소와 위험을 확인하고, 이동하는 파일을 검사한 뒤 정책에 따라 전송을 허용하거나 차단하는 방식이다.

N²SF는 국가·공공기관의 업무 정보를 기밀·민감·공개로 분류하고, 정보의 중요도와 위험 수준에 따라 보안 통제를 적용하는 체계다. 생성형 AI와 클라우드 활용이 늘어나는 환경에서 네트워크 분리뿐 아니라 보안 영역을 오가는 소프트웨어와 데이터 자체에 대한 검증도 중요해지고 있다.

‘메타디펜더 소프트웨어 공급망’은 개발·빌드·배포 과정에서 사용하는 소스코드, 외부 구성요소, 저장소, 컨테이너 등을 검사한다. 빌드는 소스코드를 실행 가능한 소프트웨어로 만드는 과정이다.

주요 기능은 소프트웨어 구성요소 분석(SCA), 여러 백신 엔진을 활용한 악성코드 검사, 취약점 진단, 소프트웨어 자재 명세서(SBOM) 생성, 비밀정보 탐지, 라이선스 검사 등이다. 구성요소를 파악하는 데 그치지 않고 악성 패키지와 취약점 등을 확인해 보안 정책에 따라 빌드·배포를 통제하도록 지원한다.

SBOM은 소프트웨어에 포함된 오픈소스와 외부 구성요소의 목록이다. 이를 통해 특정 구성요소에서 취약점이 발견됐을 때 해당 요소를 사용하는 소프트웨어를 추적할 수 있다. 제품은 SPDX와 CycloneDX 등 표준 형식을 지원한다.

소스코드에 포함된 개인정보, 비밀번호, API 키, 접근 토큰, 암호화 개인키, 클라우드 인증정보 등도 탐지한다. 깃허브·깃랩·비트버킷과 컨테이너 저장소, 지속적 통합·배포(CI/CD) 환경에 연계해 기존 개발 과정에 검증 절차를 적용할 수 있다는 설명이다.

소프트웨어와 업무 파일을 실제로 전송하는 단계에서는 ‘메타디펜더 관리형 파일 전송(MFT)’을 활용한다. 파일을 목적지로 보내기 전에 악성코드, 취약점, 민감정보 포함 여부 등을 검사하고 전송 정책을 적용한다.

여러 백신 엔진을 이용한 검사와 함께 파일의 잠재적 악성 콘텐츠를 제거하고 재구성하는 콘텐츠 무해화(CDR), 민감정보 유출 방지(DLP), 샌드박스 분석 등을 적용한다. 확장자와 실제 파일 유형이 일치하는지 확인하고 압축파일 내부도 검사한다. 외부 협력사와의 자료 교환이나 클라우드 서비스에서 들어오는 파일 등에 이러한 검증 절차를 적용할 수 있다.

보안 수준이 다른 네트워크 사이의 데이터 이동에는 교차 도메인 솔루션(CDS)과 데이터 다이오드를 활용한다. CDS는 서로 다른 보안 영역 간 데이터 반입·반출을 정책에 따라 통제하는 구조다. 사용자 인증, 전송 권한, 관리자 승인, 암호화, 파일 검사와 이동 기록 등을 연계한다.

데이터 다이오드는 하드웨어를 통해 데이터 전송 방향을 한쪽으로 제한하고 역방향 연결을 차단한다. 메타디펜더의 파일 검사 기술을 결합하면 전송 방향뿐 아니라 이동하는 파일의 위험도 함께 확인할 수 있다. 단방향 전송으로 이동 경로를 통제하고, 파일 검사로 이동 대상의 안전성을 검증하는 방식이다.

옵스왓은 개발환경과 운영환경이 분리된 정부·국방·중요 인프라에서도 소프트웨어 패키지와 빌드 결과물을 검사한 뒤 허용된 대상만 고보안 환경으로 전달하는 데 활용할 수 있다고 설명했다.

팀 유 옵스왓 GCRK 지역 영업 관리자는 “N²SF 환경에서는 소프트웨어와 파일이 보안 경계를 넘어 이동하는 모든 단계에서 무엇이 이동하는지 확인하고 안전성을 검증하며, 필요한 경우 차단하는 것이 중요하다”고 말했다.

김종광 인섹시큐리티 대표는 “실제 업무환경에서는 소프트웨어와 파일, 데이터가 지속적으로 이동하기 때문에 이동 과정에서 악성코드와 민감정보를 검증·통제할 수 있는 보안 체계가 중요하다”며 “공급망 보안부터 파일 전송, 망간 데이터 이동까지 연결해 정부·공공기관과 국방, 중요 인프라의 보안 요구에 대응하겠다”고 밝혔다.

items.summary: The cybersecurity startup plans to expand engineering and go-to-market teams in the US and UK. The post Harmonic Security Raises $50 Million for Workforce AI Protection appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
Workforce AI security startup Harmonic Security today announced raising $50 million in a Series B funding round that brings the total raised by the company to $76 million.

Founded in 2023 by Alastair Paterson (CEO) and Bryan Woolgar-O’Neil (CTO), who previously founded Digital Shadows ( acquired by ReliaQuest ), Harmonic built a platform that secures AI tools for employees.

The solution covers browser-based AI, desktop AI tools, and agentic workflows to classify every AI task, identify its use, and provide real-time control over it.

Harmonic’s expanded coverage exposes risks such as personal-account use and sensitive data exposure, among others.

The startup uses small language models to read each AI interaction in context, enabling organizations to categorize tasks, understand emerging use cases, and apply controls.

Harmonic’s Usage Intelligence layer, which offers visibility into the AI use cases that create value and improve employee workflows, uses the same engine. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

The fresh investment round was led by Crosspoint Capital Partners, with additional support from existing investors, and will help Harmonic expand its engineering and go-to-market teams in the US and UK.

“Every board I talk to is asking two questions: how do we reduce the risk of AI use, and are we getting value? Most vendors struggle to answer the first, yet we address both. From the very start, we doubled down on our custom small language models, which means we can benefit from a unique insight into enterprise AI use,” said Paterson.

The Blind Spots of Agentic Pentesting and How to Close Them
items.summary: AI-powered penetration testing can uncover complex attack paths, but safety restrictions and network limitations leave many assets and vulnerabilities untested. Picus Security explains how combining agentic pentesting with exposure validation and breach simulation can help close
items.content:
The Blind Spots of Agentic Pentesting and How to Close Them

By Sila Ozeren Hacioglu , Security Research Engineer at Picus Security.

For years, security teams had a window of several weeks between a CVE going public and attackers exploiting it. Every year, that window got smaller. Then Mythos-class models arrived, and attackers can now weaponize a new CVE within hours. That leaves security teams very little time to find out whether they’re exposed.

That’s where offensive testing comes in. But it has traditionally run on a schedule. Over the years, that schedule got tighter. Annual pentests became quarterly, and automated penetration testing tools made weekly testing possible.

Each advancement shortened the time a change could go untested. Traditional automated pentesting worked fine back when exploitation took weeks. Now that attackers have made a big jump, offensive testing is making one too.

That jump is agentic pentesting. It’s the sharp edge of offensive testing today, but it has blind spots. This piece looks at where they are and how to close them.

A manual pentest usually goes through several phases: reconnaissance, vulnerability assessment, initial access, post-exploitation, and reporting. Traditional automated pentesting tools follow the same phases. Even before LLMs took off, some advanced tools used machine learning to choose the next step. For example, five years ago, we built our Attack Path Validation (APV) product with such a decision engine. But AI agents take it further.

In agentic pentesting, one or more AI agents carry out a pentest step by step. In our agentic pentesting product , Picus Swarm uses five specialist agents orchestrated by Numi AI.

AI pentest agents evaluate findings and your organization’s context to choose the next step dynamically. That creativity lets them find exploit chains much faster than a human pentester, including some a human might miss entirely. However, creativity comes at a cost.

Running everything agentically uses a lot of tokens, and results vary from run to run. Even when nothing has changed in the environment, an agent can fail to exploit a vulnerability five times and succeed on the sixth. Running dozens of tests to be sure gets expensive, and in a large organization with thousands of endpoints, a single agentic run can take weeks.

That’s why deterministic automated pentesting is still needed . It’s less creative, but it delivers consistent testing, costs less, and finishes faster, so it can run far more often. It follows repeatable steps, allowing teams to compare runs over time and reliably retest fixes.

The right approach offers both. Run deterministic tests often for predictable coverage and agentic tests at set intervals. How often depends on your organization’s needs and risk appetite. Picus Autonomous Pentesting can run in either mode, fully agentic or deterministic, and adapts to your context, risks, and changes in the threat landscape and your environment.

Agentic pentesting is valuable, and the need for it is real. But it has limits worth understanding.

See What Your Pentesting Covers, and What It Doesn’t

In most deployments, automated pentesting covers only one of six surfaces you need to validate.

This whitepaper shows what stays untested, from detection rules to cloud, identity, and AI guardrails, why adding AI doesn’t lift that ceiling, and three questions that expose the gap.

The Achilles’ Heel of Agentic Pentesting: Untestable Assets and Exposures

Agentic pentesting’s biggest strength is also its limit. It tests by running real attacks, so it can only test what it can safely reach. Omdia research found that organizations pentest only 32% of their attack surface on average .
